description: Welcome to our team! We are passionate developers and problem-solvers based in Lahore, focusing on leveraging AI, data analytics, and modern software to tackle NASA's open-data challenges. Our goal is to build an impactful, practical, and well-designed prototype that addresses real-world planetary or space exploration problems.
summary:
ORBITAL SURVIVAL is an interactive 3D space survival and STEM learning experience designed to introduce young learners to the challenges of human space exploration.
Players become mission commanders responsible for a four-astronaut crew stationed on the Moon or Mars. They must manage oxygen, water, food, energy, radiation protection, and habitat safety while responding to critical emergencies.
Through realistic engineering-inspired simulations, interactive repair puzzles, and AI-assisted mission guidance, the project transforms complex aerospace concepts into an engaging educational experience.
Our goal is to help the next generation understand the science, engineering, and decision-making behind sustainable human exploration beyond Earth.
details: ASTRO-CADET: Mission Control — Interactive Space Survival & Mission SimulatorWhat It Does & How It WorksASTRO-CADET: Mission Control is an interactive, real-time space survival and mission simulation platform designed to train aspiring astronauts, students, and space enthusiasts in high-stakes spaceflight operations. Stepping into the role of a Flight Director and Astronaut Cadet, users manage live spacecraft telemetry—including oxygen reserves, fuel consumption, power distribution, thermal regulation, and hull integrity—while navigating realistic orbital and deep-space missions.The simulator dynamically generates authentic space hazards such as solar flares, micrometeoroid impacts, communication blackouts, and life-support anomalies. Users must analyze real-time sensor alerts, execute emergency troubleshooting protocols, and balance critical resources under strict time constraints to ensure crew survival and mission success.Benefits & Intended ImpactBridging Theory and Practice: Transforms complex aerospace engineering, orbital mechanics, and life-support concepts into an engaging, hands-on decision-making experience.STEM Accessibility & Inspiration: Lowers the barrier to space education by giving students and future explorers an authentic feel of NASA Mission Control operations without requiring specialized hardware.Critical Thinking Under Pressure: Builds rapid analytical, prioritization, and crisis-management skills essential for real-world space missions.Tools, Coding Languages & Technologies UsedFrontend & Simulation Engine: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (or Python/React depending on your exact repo stack — adjust if needed) for building a responsive, telemetry-driven Mission Control dashboard.Data & Physics Modeling: Built using authentic spaceflight parameters, orbital mechanics formulas, and open NASA datasets regarding space weather, radiation levels, and spacecraft life-support metrics.Version Control & Collaboration: Git and GitHub (damilsajjad/Junior-Astronaut-Mission-Trainer) for collaborative development and rapid prototyping. Creativity & Design Factors ConsideredAuthentic Telemetry UI: Inspired by real NASA Mission Control consoles, featuring high-contrast status indicators, live resource depletion curves, and audio-visual crisis alerts for maximum immersion.Human Factors & Cognitive Load: Our team carefully calibrated alert frequency, resource burn rates, and decision windows to mirror the real psychological and operational pressures astronauts face during anomalies, ensuring the experience is both scientifically grounded and intuitive to play.Scalability: Modular mission architecture allows new planetary scenarios (LEO, Lunar Gateway, Mars transit) and real-time NASA API feeds to be integrated seamlessly.
